headline: 15,000+ passengers affected as 103 Dhaka-Saudi flights cancelled
summary: Flight disruptions at King Khalid and Dammam international airports following Houthi attacks have left thousands of travelers in limbo.
details: Over 15,779 passengers have been affected by the cancellation and disruption of 103 international flights between Dhaka and Saudi Arabia.
The chaos was triggered by the closure of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Dammam International Airport following attacks by Houthi rebels.
According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the disruptions include 42 direct flights and 61 transit flights.
Among the direct flights, Biman Bangladesh Airlines had 17 cancelled, US-Bangla Airlines 10, Saudia 8, and Airways 7.
Transit disruptions affected several carriers, including 22 flights from IndiGo, 14 from Emirates, 8 from Qatar Airways, and others from flydubai, Air India, and EgyptAir.
The sudden cancellations have caused extreme uncertainty and hardship for thousands of expatriate workers, as well as those traveling for Hajj and Umrah.
CAAB stated that they are maintaining constant communication with relevant airlines and airport authorities to normalize the situation.
caption:
Over 15,000 passengers stranded as 103 flights between Dhaka and Saudi Arabia are cancelled.

Over 15,779 passengers have been affected by the cancellation and disruption of 103 international flights between Dhaka and Saudi Arabia.

The chaos was triggered by the closure of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Dammam International Airport following attacks by Houthi rebels.

According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh (CAAB), the disruptions include 42 direct flights and 61 transit flights.

Among the direct flights, Biman Bangladesh Airlines had 17 cancelled, US-Bangla Airlines 10, Saudia 8, and Airways 7.

Transit disruptions affected several carriers, including 22 flights from IndiGo, 14 from Emirates, 8 from Qatar Airways, and others from flydubai, Air India, and EgyptAir.

The sudden cancellations have caused extreme uncertainty and hardship for thousands of expatriate workers, as well as those traveling for Hajj and Umrah.

CAAB stated that they are maintaining constant communication with relevant airlines and airport authorities to normalize the situation.

headline: 28 dead as school roof collapse kills students in Pakistan
summary: At least 27 students and one teacher were killed in Peshawar after a higher floor collapsed onto classrooms.
details: At least 27 students, most under 13, and one teacher were killed on Thursday when a school roof collapsed in Peshawar, Pakistan.
The incident occurred at the private Al-Khair Education Center in Dir Colony while students were being taught in class.
Rescue officials stated that the roof of a higher floor collapsed onto the first floor, which then fell on the students in their classrooms.
Hospital spokesperson Mohammad Asim reported that 20 others were wounded and brought to Lady Reading Hospital.
District emergency officer Iftikhar Khan said at least 45 children have been retrieved from the rubble, with fears that more may still be buried.
Rescue teams continue to work on shifting bodies and the injured to hospitals as the death toll is feared to rise.
caption:
28 people, mostly children under 13, killed in a school roof collapse in Pakistan.

Hospital spokesperson Mohammad Asim reported that 20 others were wounded and brought to Lady Reading Hospital.

District emergency officer Iftikhar Khan said at least 45 children have been retrieved from the rubble, with fears that more may still be buried.
